summary: Anthropic's Claude Code coding agent, driven in a terminal.

manual.$comment: Claude Code's default mode: it asks before edits and commands. A chat adds a hook that asks before the commands it would otherwise judge read-only too; a terminal agent gets the CLI's own default mode.
manual.label: Manual
manual.description: Claude Code’s asking mode: it asks before every edit and every command it does not already know to be safe. In a chat, every action that changes something or reaches out asks; reading and searching the workspace does not.

acceptEdits.$comment: Claude Code's own Accept edits mode, at the Auto level: what Auto meant for Claude until Auto became its classifier (owner ruling 2026-10-01), still there for a person who wants edits through and every command asked.
acceptEdits.label: Accept edits
acceptEdits.description: Claude Code’s Accept edits mode: file edits in the workspace go through without asking, and commands ask first.

auto.$comment: The CLI's own classifier mode (owner ruling 2026-10-01): a person who picks Auto for Claude expects Claude's auto mode, and acceptEdits asked before every command. Where the account or model is not offered the classifier, the CLI starts in its asking mode instead.
auto.label: Auto
auto.summary: Claude runs what it judges safe; blocks the rest.
auto.description: Claude Code’s own auto mode: a classifier runs the tool calls it judges safe and turns the risky ones back to Claude. Where your plan or model does not offer it, Claude asks instead.

dontAsk.$comment: Claude Code's own Don't ask mode: it never asks, and refuses whatever the person's allow rules do not already cover. At the Manual level, since nothing outside those rules runs.
dontAsk.label: Don’t ask
dontAsk.summary: Never asks; refuses what your rules don’t allow.
dontAsk.description: Claude Code’s Don’t ask mode: it never stops to ask, and turns down every tool call your own allow rules do not already cover.

bypass.label: Bypass permissions
bypass.summary: Skips every prompt. Trusted repos only.
bypass.description: Claude Code’s Bypass permissions mode: no prompts at all. Use only in repositories and environments you trust.

reasoningSelection.$comment: claude --effort <level>, documented in --help on CLI 2.1.220. No default is declared: the CLI's own default effort is undocumented, so declaring one would have to be a guess, and an incorrect guess silently changes launches. Omitting it means a blank selection passes no flag and every explicitly picked level does.

launchSettings.$comment: claude --settings '<json>', verified against the installed CLI 2.1.268 on 2026-09-11 and documented as applying above the user, project and local settings files and below managed settings, writing nothing to disk. It carries what a plugin cannot: Claude Code's plugin settings.json accepts only `agent` and `subagentStatusLine`, so the status line the app reads context usage, cost and lines-changed from must arrive here. The theme rides the same document rather than a second --settings, whose repeatability is undocumented.

launchPlugins.$comment: claude --plugin-dir <dir>, verified against the installed CLI 2.1.268 on 2026-09-11: a directory passed this way loads its skills, its hooks/hooks.json and its .mcp.json for THAT SESSION ONLY — `claude mcp list` shows the server as plugin:<name>:<server> with the flag and not without it, and nothing is written to ~/.claude or to the project. The flag is repeatable and must name each plugin directory: pointing it at the marketplace root (the directory holding .claude-plugin/marketplace.json) loaded neither child plugin. Hook commands in a plugin may use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, and the launch env reaches the hook process, which is how the reporter finds its socket.

promptInjection.$comment: The first message goes after `--`, so one that starts with a dash is never read as an option. Checked 2026-10-22 against Claude Code 2.1.296: `claude --help` prints `Usage: claude [options] [command] [prompt]`, `claude --bogus` failed with `unknown option`, and `claude -- --bogus` took `--bogus` as the prompt.

overflow.$comment: A first message too long for the platform's command line (a pasted log; see src/main/launch-arg-budget.ts) is typed in instead: the launch drops it and the host pastes it, bracketed, then presses Enter once the TUI is reading. Verified 2026-09-24 against the installed CLI 2.1.282: --help documents no prompt-file option and no stdin prompt for an interactive session (--input-format and piped stdin apply only with --print), and a 300 KB bracketed paste followed by Enter, written once output had gone quiet after the TUI enabled bracketed paste, was submitted as one message and answered once.

contextInjection.$comment: claude --append-system-prompt-file <path>, verified against the installed CLI 2.1.263: the options list documents --append-system-prompt, and --bare's own text names the file variant as --append-system-prompt[-file]. A FILE rather than the text because the host-context document is multi-line markdown, and argv is not where a document belongs. Spread into launch AND resume argv, so a resumed session is re-told what the host said.

launchIntegration.$comment: The person's synced MCP servers ride `--mcp-config <file>` beside --plugin-dir, and the knowledge-activity hook joins the one --settings document. Measured against Claude Code 2.1.296 on 2026-10-16: a --mcp-config server starts with no approval prompt, merges with the project's and the person's servers and wins on the same id; --settings hooks fire beside the project's and every plugin's; a second --settings replaces the first outright, so everything goes in one.

installTargets.$comment: restartRequired verified false on 2026-07-29: a skill directory created while `claude` was already running appeared in its /skill picker without a restart. kimi-claude and zai run the same `claude` binary against the same .claude/skills, so the finding covers all three.

agentStateSpec.$comment: Authoritative agent-state via Claude Code lifecycle hooks, merged as tagged entries into the workspace settings. PreToolUse is register:false deliberately: PreToolUse and PostToolUse fire once per tool call each, and PostToolUse alone is load-bearing (its thinking frame is the only signal that clears awaiting_input after a permission is answered), so registering only PostToolUse halves the per-tool reporter spawns. The Notification allow-list keeps informational types (idle_prompt, auth_success, elicitation_complete/response, agent_completed — documented set as of 2026-07-08) from parking a session as falsely needs-input forever (the 2026-07-07 incident); if a future Claude build adds a new BLOCKING notification_type, extend oneOf here. FileChanged (Claude Code 2.1.266) is registered for the agent CHANGELIST, not the phase: its payload is file_path + event (change|add|unlink) with no diff, so the reporter forwards it as a path-only touch and an edit made through Bash, a formatter or codegen still reaches the ledger at file level. It fires ONLY for paths a hook has armed with hookSpecificOutput.watchPaths — nothing arms any today, so it is declared register:false: the reporter already reads the event, and the day something arms watch paths the registration is one flag away. Two reasons it stays unwritten until that arming is decided: arming a whole repository would spawn a reporter per file change (a git checkout is thousands), and the declared phase is `thinking` only because the event table requires one — a watcher event firing while the session was idle would move the phase, which is the wrong kind of wrong.
